ai.title: Freebuff CLI 1.0.542 release with local agents toggle and startup
ai.summary: Version 1.0.542 of the codebuff package ships with two CLI refactors: the local agents display toggle was removed from `cli/src/app.tsx` (users should use the `@` command instead), and eager agent validation during CLI startup in `index.tsx` was replaced with lazy validation inside `useAgentValidation`. This simplifies component prop drilling by removing `loadedAgentsData` and `validationErrors` from App and Chat, and filters network errors before setting validation state.
ai.evidence: Diff shows a single line change in `cli/release/package.json` incrementing the `codebuff` package version from 1.0.541 to 1.0.542. Analysis notes confirm this is a release-bump commit with no other source changes, and list two preceding minor refactors to the CLI agent display and validation logic as part of this release.

eli5.text: Freebuff CLI 1.0.542 streamlines agent management by removing the built-in local agents toggle from the interface. The CLI now uses the '@' command for agent switching instead of a dedicated toggle, simplifying how you interact with built-in agents. Startup is faster and cleaner because agent validation no longer runs automatically during launch; it only checks when needed, reducing delays and avoiding redundant background work. Network errors are now filtered out during validation, so you are less likely to see confusing error messages when an agent check fails due to a temporary connection issue. Upgrading makes the CLI more responsive at launch and gives you a more straightforward, command-driven way to manage and switch between agents.

ai.title: CLI logo sheen animation loop and deduplication
ai.summary: Refactored CLI logo rendering to use a shared `useLogo` hook with dynamic sheen animation. Removed duplicate `getSheenColor` from `login-modal-utils.ts` and updated `use-sheen-animation.tsx` to support looping fill/unfill effects using theme colors. Scope: `cli/src/app.tsx`, `cli/src/hooks/use-logo.tsx`, `cli/src/hooks/use-sheen-animation.tsx`, `cli/src/login/utils.ts`.

eli5.text: When you open the CLI, the logo now shows a smooth green shimmer that glides across it and then loops again, like a light sweeping over the brand mark. The animation logic lives in one shared place, so the login screen and the main app draw it the same way instead of carrying two copies of the same code. You won't see the sweep only once and stop, it repeats, and the green matches the app’s new green-themed look. The effect is visible now anywhere the logo appears in the terminal.

Logo rendering was refactored onto a shared `useLogo` hook with a looping fill/unfill sheen animation, and the duplicate `getSheenColor` utility was dropped from `login-modal-utils.ts`. These visual upgrades make the tool more pleasant to use every day, with consistent branding and smoother animations that improve the overall flow of your coding sessions.

ai.title: code-search filters non-existent hidden dirs
ai.summary: The code search tool now filters hidden directories via fs.statSync before passing them to ripgrep. This prevents stderr errors from ripgrep complaining about non-existent paths. The change is isolated to sdk/src/tools/code-search.ts. Only blessed hidden directories that actually exist in the search CWD are included in the arguments.

eli5.text: When you use the code search tool, it now quietly skips over hidden folders that don't actually exist on your machine before sending the search request. You would notice this indirectly - the error messages about missing or invalid paths in your terminal's error output should stop appearing altogether. This mainly affects anyone actively searching files using the SDK's built-in code search feature, who previously might have seen cryptic warnings about non-existent directories cluttering their output.

ai.title: Update manifold eval with initCommand and finalCheckCommands
ai.summary: Added initCommand and finalCheckCommands fields to evals/buffbench/eval-manifold.json. initCommand runs yarn install and restores yarn.lock. finalCheckCommands executes TypeScript compilation and build steps across common, backend/api, backend/scheduler, backend/shared, and web packages. This ensures proper environment setup and validation during manifold benchmark evaluations.

eli5.text: When Manifold's automated code-checking tool runs on the Manifold Markets repository, it now first installs all the necessary packages and restores the project's dependency file before doing any testing, and then runs a series of build-and-check steps to make sure the code compiles correctly across different parts of the application. Previously, the tool skipped the setup step and jumped straight into evaluation, which could lead to incomplete or error-prone results; now, the checks run against a properly prepared environment, producing more reliable benchmark assessments of how well an AI model performs on this codebase.

ai.title: Log codebuff runner errors in evals
ai.summary: Added error logging to CodebuffRunner in `evals/buffbench/runners/codebuff.ts`. Captures `result.output.type === 'error'` events to `console.error` with commit/agent IDs. When `DEBUG_ERROR` is set, writes full output and trace to a JSON file in the parent directory. Internal observability improvement for buffbench evals.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs into a problem during testing, the system now writes a note about it down in the error log so the testing team can see what went wrong. If a special debug setting is turned on, it also saves the full details of the problem into a file. The problem it watches for is when the assistant reports back that something failed unexpectedly.

ai.title: Append tool error messages after all tool results
ai.summary: Tool error messages in stream-parser.ts now collect into a separate array and append after toolResultsToAddAfterStream. Anthropic API requires tool results to immediately follow the assistant message with tool calls; previously, error messages interleaved with tool results broke this ordering.

eli5.text: When the assistant tried to use a tool and something went wrong, the error explanation used to get mixed in between the other tool answers. Now those error explanations wait in line and get added only after all the tool answers have been collected. If you watched the assistant handle a failed tool call, you would see the error message appear at the end of the group instead of jumping ahead of the results it followed. This keeps the message order correct so the conversation keeps moving smoothly.

ai.title: Unify agent tool input schema with spawnagents structure
ai.summary: Refactored agent tool input schemas to use nested `prompt` and `params` fields, matching the `spawn_agents` structure instead of flattening parameters. This change updates `buildAgentToolInputSchema` in `packages/agent-runtime/src/templates/prompts.ts` and removes the `getZodObjectShape` helper. `tryTransformAgentToolCall` in `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/tool-executor.ts` now passes existing `prompt`/`params` directly without reconstruction. Documentation in `common/src/tools/params/tool/spawn-agents.ts` reflects the unified schema.

eli5.text: When you ask an AI agent to do something using direct tool calls (not the spawn_agents method), the system now handles the input the same way it always has for spawn_agents. This means the prompt and parameters are treated consistently whether you invoke an agent directly or through the batch endpoint. You won't notice any visible difference in how agents run, but internally the code is now simpler and less error-prone because it doesn't have to reconstruct or reformat the input data. The change is live today and applies to all agent tool calls.

ai.title: BuffBench judge errors log full output and write debug files
ai.summary: Judge error handling in evals/buffbench/judge.ts now logs the full structured output alongside the trace. A DEBUG_ERROR flag writes failed judge outputs to JSON files named by commit ID and agent ID. The judgeCommitResult interface accepts an EvalCommitV2 object instead of separate prompt and groundTruthFileDiffs arguments. Callers in run-buffbench.ts updated to pass the full commit object.

eli5.text: When an AI assistant in internal testing gets confused and produces garbled or malformed responses, the system now captures the full picture of what went wrong instead of just a brief note. Previously, only a short trace of the failure was logged. Now, the complete structured output and the error trace are both recorded together, and detailed copies of failed outputs are saved as files named after the specific commit and AI agent involved. This means whoever investigates these failures will have all the information they need to understand why a particular test case broke, rather than having to piece it together from partial clues.
